query.explanation: Table and column names cannot be bound as parameters, so dynamic SQL must quote them. format with %I applies identifier quoting, wrapping the name in double quotes and doubling any embedded double quotes.
query.title: format('%I') for identifiers

questions.prompt: When a LIKE pattern comes from a bound parameter, which characters still keep special meaning?

The driver escapes nothing inside the value; LIKE still interprets the pattern metacharacters after binding.

query.explanation: Binding stops a value from altering SQL structure, but the LIKE operator still interprets % and _ inside the pattern it receives. Unescaped wildcards from users cause over-broad matching, so escape them with an ESCAPE clause when an exact substring is intended.

con.executemany("insert into t values (?)", [("a",), ("b",)])
